item.title: Wagers
item.description:
A Wager refers to the act of spending 1 SP to add a +Dice to your roll in Combat or otherwise. You must declare a Wager before the first die is rolled, but you may wait until you know all the applied modifiers.
When rolling with a Wager placed, any Critical rolled (1 or 12) will Burn your wagered SP. SP that are not Burnt are moved aside and will be recovered after a Sanctuary Rest.

item.title: Specialties
item.description:
When creating a Player Character, pick 1 of the Specialties below. You may take extra Specialties at the cost of +1 SP per Specialty known.
Ex. your 2nd Specialty is 2 SP, 4th is 4 SP, so on and so forth. Specialties help anchoring the Narrative and Storytelling part of the game, without adding unnecessary numerical bloat.

item.title: Sanctuary Rest
item.description: Places safe from both environmental (weather, terrain) and creature-based threats. It should ideally have some form of enrichment or activity (a library, a forge, etc.). Resting here restores full HP and Armor Pips and grants milestone SP (extra SP from enriched locations).Sanctuary Checklist: Friendly? (No Hostiles around that are aware of you) Comfortable? (Bedrolls, thick moss, pillows, a comfy pile of hay) Secured? (Easily Defended, preferably guarded) Insulated? (Safe from the weather and climate) Sanctified? (Against Intrusions) Provisioned? (Food, drink, rations) Unsafe Spots: Resting in an unsafe location (ones that don't meet 4/6 of the above requirements) carries risk (ambush, robbery, etc.). It only restores half of your max HP and Armor Pips and does not grant SP. If you set up a guard duty, those on watch do not gain the benefits of the rest at all.

item.title: Resolution
item.description: When you wish to undertake an action with a degree of probability or tension included (picking a lock, overhearing a conversation), you roll a single d12 as the base, then apply any +Dice and/or -Dice modifiers, and consult the table below:

item.title: Aether Sickness
item.description: Aether represents perfect reality and the balance of nature. Over-absorption overwhelms the soul. Characters can only benefit from Aether-Magic healing up to half their Max HP per Sanctuary Rest. Beyond the Cap: Roll a d12 whenever you are healed by Aether. First instance beyond the cap: Sickness only on a roll of 1. Each subsequent instance: Increase the failure range by your Max HP. (e.g., a character with 5 Max HP fails on a 1-6 on their second healing instance beyond the cap). Effects: When subject to Aether Sickness, you enter a catatonic state, inversing the Heroic Bleedout state - Losing 2x AP per HP over 0. (A character with 3 HP, when sick, would lose 6 AP). The Sickness passes after you’ve gone into negative AP, or HP, as you violently rid your system of the excess Aether, usually through puking.

item.title: Vitals
item.description: The amount of Hits a Player character can take. Called that to distinguish from AER Monster Rules HP.

item.title: Speed
item.description: The maximum amount of Hexes a Character can move by paying 1 AP.

item.title: Skill Points
item.description: A meta-currency, gained after reaching a milestone AND taking a Sanctuary Rest. Can be spent on learning new Skill instances, improving known ones, or on Wagers.

item.title: Focus Points
item.description: Sub-currency gained on successful melee attacks and receiving DMG. By default, Player characters can have up to 6 FP stored, and may spend it to help pay for Skills (up to half a Skill's total cost).

item.title: Armour
item.description: Armour is an extra layer of HP/Vitals. It will take damage before them, and is divided into Physical and Magical Armour types, stopping the appropriate types of DMG. Usually gained through equipment and Skills, but may be INNATE for some Races.

item.title: Action Points
item.description:
The most important currency in Combat.
By default, Player characters have 12 AP max, and start Combat with as much, then regenerate as much as their Race and/or Skills indicate at the start of their Turn.

item.title: Turn
item.description: Part of a Round. Enemies take theirs in a set order, while Players may intervene between those, either one at a time, or all together. Regardless, unless specified otherwise, each creature can only take One Turn per Round.

item.title: Resistance
item.description: Reduces incoming DMG of a given type by 1, to no set minimum. With enough Resistance and/or Immunity added together regenerating Vitals, or HP from certain attacks or Skills is possible.

item.title: Reaction
item.description: Spending AP, or in the case of Enemies Dominance Points to act outside one's Turn, usually during another creature's action and on being provided a Trigger of sorts - Ex. being attacked, someone moving past your Hex, etc.

item.title: Immunity
item.description: Reduces incoming DMG of a given type to 0. Applies before Resistance.

item.title: Heroic Bleedout
item.description:
State activated when Vitals drop below 0. In this state you lose 2 AP Regen for every 1 Vitals below 0. Should your Stored AP reach 0 (either by being taken away through negative Regen, or by one last action), your character Dies.
Alternative: Damsely Faint - when reduced below 0 Vitals you may instead choose to Faint, thus be removed from the Combat and hope your companions can finish the fight without you. Less risk of losing your character, but less agency in what happens next. Great for a bathroom break.

item.title: Cover
item.description: Gives -Dice on ranged attacks and Skills regardless of distance. Usually provided by terrain and/or map objects, as well as other creatures.

item.title: DMG
item.description:
When a Skill's effect deals magical damage, select one of the following types for it. Aether - Magical.
Entropy - Physical.
Fire - Magical.
Ice - Physical.
Psychic - Magical.
Thunder - Magical.

item.title: Thunder
item.description: Thunder: On a successful roll, 1 damage arcs to one additional target within 2 hexes.

item.title: Ice
item.description: Ice: Deals Physical damage and applies a stack of Brittle. The next Skill or Attack made against a Brittle enemy gets +Dice.

item.title: Fire
item.description: Fire: Can ignite unarmoured targets on a successful roll, dealing 1 additional damage at the start of their next turn. This can continue each turn on a successful roll.

item.title: Entropy
item.description: Entropy: Deals Physical Damage, and does 1 additional damage to exposed Health (Hit Points/Vitals).

item.title: Aether
item.description: Aether: Deals double damage to Undead and Daemons, but heals any other target. Healing through Aether Skills is subject to Aether Sickness.

item.title: Dryad ♙ - ♣️ + ♠️
item.description: Bloom Restore 2 HP to an adjacent Overgrowth ally, including the Dryad. Swing Pull the Dryad towards another Overgrowth ally within 6 Hexes. The Dryad can end the Swing on ANY Hex adjacent to the Swing target. Slash Move up to 2 Hexes and deal 1 Physical DMG and 1 Entropy DMG. Javelin Throw a ranged projectile at a creature up to 6 Hexes away. You may Swing to that projectile on the same Turn. Shriek Deal 2 Psychic DMG to a creature that damages an Overgrowth ally, including the Dryad. Can be used as a reaction. 2x Weak to Fire 3x Resistant to Entropy 49d0f8f03b35264cef5e6a70042ae590.jpg747cd3c17ff280964483ed57817dbfde (1).jpg

item.title: Earthshaper ♕ - ♦️ + ♠️
item.description: Reshape Terrain For every 1 AC spent Influence one Hex of terrain that the Earthshaper can see in one of the following ways: Erect wall (+1 Elevation). Create Pit (-1 Elevation). Difficult Terrain (+1 AP movement cost). Move any previously created feature by 1 Hex. Leap Move 3 Hexes in any direction, regardless of elevation. Earth Armour Destroy a Hex of nearby Elevation to regain 5 PA. Vegetation Armour Destroy a Hex of nearby Difficult Terrain to regain 3 MA. Maul Deal 6 Physical DMG. If the Earthshaper is the only creature that can see the target, it deals an extra 3 Psychic DMG. Ram Jump down on the target, dealing 3 Physical DMG per level of Elevation change. Ex. Jumping Wall -> Ground would deal 3 DMG, while Wall -> Pit would result in 6 DMG. Unstoppable momentum The next Ram deals DMG to all adjacent Hexes as well. Regeneration Restore 3 HP, 2 PA, and 1 MA. Any Excess HP restoration is split evenly between PA and MA. c1e3ebe23c1534fa6015d1711e015ea2.jpg

item.title: Giant ♕ - ♥️ + ♥️
item.description: Stomp deal 2 (3) DMG. Target's movement costs +1 AP next time they move. Kick Deal 1 (2) DMG. Displace target by 3 Hexes. {Swing} Deal 4 DMG in a 3 Hex line originating from the Giant. Deal 1 (2) DMG in a 5 Hex Cone originating from the Giant. Grab / Toss Pick up an adjacent creature or terrain feature. The Giant has +Dice on this contest the first time it uses this Action Cluster. If a creature/terrain piece is already grabbed, instead, Toss it up to 6 Hexes away. The tossed creature/terrain piece, and any creature standing on the landing spot takes 3 Physical DMG. A grabbed creature may free itself by dealing 5 DMG to the Giant between its turns. 2x Resistant to Physical Variants: (X) - Armoured Giant {X} - Armed Giant Rampage Deal 1 (2) DMG to all adjacent Hexes. dfaf9bb876954eadcb06a58936553a65.jpg

item.title: Hydra ♕ - ♥️ + ♦️
item.description: Turn Flip its token in place, turning around. Rush Move 1 Hex and attack for 1 Physical DMG for every 10 Max HP. Stampede Move 3 Hexes in a straight line, dealing 1 Physical DMG to all creatures passed. Bite Attack for 1 Physical DMG for every 10 Max HP, 3x Attacks per use of this AC. Each attack can be aimed individually. 2x Weak to Fire Head Regrowth: Gain +3 Max HP and +2 AC for every 3 DMG taken from the front (wider side). (ex. 8 AC 27/33 HP -> 10 AC 24/36 HP -> etc.). Rejuvenate Restore 5 HP per DA spent. Thrash Deal 1 Physical DMG to all adjacent creatures. download 1.jpg

item.description: Points provide both a secondary layer of Vitals and a DMG reduction stat (min 1). DMGR applied before Armour takes DMG. DMGR = CURRENT Armour Points Resistance works only on Vitals, then? Immunity + Resistance = Heal 1? (Reduce to 0 + Reduce by 1 = -1 = Heal 1?) Arrows - 3x1 inventory space, stack up to 5 arrows in a bundle. Arrow Quiver - 3x2 inventory space, fits up to 30 arrows. (Alternative is having 10 Arrows in the same amount of space without one). Crossbow Bolt - 2x1 inventory space, stack up to 5. Crossbow Quiver - 2x2 inventory space, fits up to 30. (Alternative is having 10 Bolts in the same amount of space without one). Firearm Bullet - 1x1 inventory space, stacks up to 5. Bullet Pouch - 2x1 inventory space, holds up to 30. (Alternative is having 10 Bullets in the same amount of space without one). Normal is normal. "Heavy X": -2 Max Range, +1 DMG (made with 2x materials) "Poison X": -1 Movement on Hit (made with Herbs/Mushrooms) "Birdshot Firearm Ammo": Cone hitzone at half listed range (Made with different materials) Healing item, drawing a weapon, switching ammo, stowing something. On the grid: 2 AP In a Bag: 4 AP Names are Exonyms (given by others for identification and familiarity). Names<Titles. Concepts>Function. Prefix "Aelf". Material can play a role. Ex.: Aelf-Obsidian, Aelf-Artifice, or The Artificer. The Apex Aelf-Silence Aelf-Dogma The Thing Names are industrial and purpose-driven. Jobs and assignments over substance. Colour or other distinct features can play a role. Sometimes longer words erode into nicks (can also signal affection or independence from the Spire). Ex.: Tink (from Tinker) Runner Jane (from Janitor) Rad (from Radio) Cass (from Casing/Casting) They are defined by their fall. They have titles that need to be claimed through action, declarations that need fulfillment to count. Ex.: Malice Sorrow Alienation Murder Husk The Demagogue The Heretic The Usurper Names related to minerals, ore, metals, using many harsh and hard sounds (like G, R, K, Z, X, Y). Tough to pronounce for everyone else, so socialite Yig names erode into softer, easier to pronounce and remember names, "Kryzx" may become "Clicks". Ex.: Krakk (Crack) Zygax Grux (Cruz) Xyrok (Rock) Kygroz Yigvrese being the "Official" name for their kind, similarly to "Homo Sapiens", rarely sees use. The representatives refer to their kin as a shortened Yigg, which was adapted widely for being less of a mouthful. Reducing them to a terms such as "Diggers" may come off as mean. Scandinavian/Swedish names, particularly ones ending in -son, putting emphasis on their ancestry and elders. Ex.: Hemingson Ragisson Gamlisson Anson Paulsen Kristoffersen Ottosen Olofsonn Calling them Furries drives them crazy, in the wrong sense. Also disrespect to lineage is non-tolerable (omitting the -son). Either directly descriptive names alluding to their traits or appearance, or common names shared between humans and domesticated animals Ex.: Daisy Diego Fluffer Paws Wagger Chaser Cupcake They seem to have a deaf ear for any negative nicks or insults thrown their way, so long as they know they're the ones being addressed. True names are stereotypically fire-related (ex. Coal, Spark, Bright), but those living in Sanctuaries often adapt a common first name to pair it with, resulting in a first name + surname structure Ex.: Bob Spark Norman Bright Ada Burns Frank Coal John Wick They may treat being addressed as their True names as insulting or endearing depending on the speaker and surroundings. The Spires are not united. They share a goal (profit and domination) but are cutthroat, even with each other. They engage in open fights over resources or sabotage. However, they must collaborate, as their services are essential to each other and expensive. Longhorn and MGM - McGriff Mining. Provide materials for the others, at harsh prices. (Destroyed) Derelict and Bröninger. Scattered throught the Spires, making weaponry and processing materials from McGriff. Brighthouse and CMT - Control, Maintain, Transport. Control The Ledger, and hold the others back with benefits from all three, as everyone understands the need for solidarity, at least on the surface. RF - Reclamation Forces. High-tech pest control / Intrusion specialists / hazardous materials crew / critical asset extraction team. They're not there to "Win", but to solve the issue at hand, even if its putting a Band-Aid on exposed bone. Vs Overgrowth - Purge Squads. Equipped with flamers and chemical defoliants. Vs The Bad Moon - Anchor Squads. They can't fight The Moon, but they will bolt themselves to the ground and fire as many Shell Piercing rounds as it takes to protect their escort if need be. Vs The Deep - Sanity Squads. More of an intel and precaution branch as once the effects set in, the location is lost anyway. Vs Shimmer - Disposal Squads. Tasked with locating and relocating the Heart, while breaking as much of the surface as they can on their way there. RF - Reclamation Corps. The subtler twin handling records that need erasing and mouths that should have really stopped talking a few sentences ago. Cloudline and US - Updraft Systems. Secretly hostile towards McGriff and responsible for Air Superiority near Spire territory. Economy: "NeoMoney" and the Role of CMT Currency: NeoHumans have their own "currency" that doesn't exist elsewhere. It's not cash, but an internal ledger system based on a "complex equation". The Equation: Value is determined by CMT and based on raw materials, technology, research, assets, workforce, and personal scores to settle. CMT's Control: CMT (the "Control" faction) literally controls the value of everything. They are the central bank and the police, rolled into one. This "currency" is their leash. They can arbitrarily devalue a Spire's industry (e.g., heavy machinery, hurting Longhorn) to keep everyone in check. External: The currency is worthless to outsiders. Trade with the rest of Jaddivar is done via barter of the actual goods (guns, materials, transport). Co-dependent Animosity The Delicate Balance: CMT is the head, but it can't afford to kill the body (Longhorn, Updraft) that feeds it. This creates a fragile cooperativeness. The Secret: This internal hatred and co-dependence is the Spires' most closely guarded secret, worth billions of NeoMoney, and heavily censored by Starchart. Conflict: This is a cold war fought with spreadsheets, sabotage, and corporate espionage. Conflicts are "aggressive asset acquisitions". Lives lost are just logged "manpower," a replaceable asset in the grand equation. Adventurers are not in any books, unaccounted for, not evaluated, and completely deniable - making them the perfect solution for desperate situations. Groups that do regular work for a Spire can get standing with it, represented with gear, trust, and better work for better pay, but it can all fall apart at one wrong step as the execs pull out. Rival Spires can also consider you an "on-sight" threat at the higher levels of standing. Double crossing a Spire will have CMT send out a squad for both the assets that still need recovering, and the traitorous adventurers. Spires vs. Saurians: Relationship: Actively Hostile. Open conflict. Saurian Perspective: Spires are an existential threat, a plague, arrogant as the Starborn. Spire Perspective: Saurians are "hostile indigenous fauna," an obstacle, a "Class-B Threat" that's just sitting on resource nodes. Spires vs. Sanctuary Cities: Relationship: Tense, Pragmatic Neutrality. Purely transactional. Dynamic: The "Switzerland" of Jaddivar. "Check your wars at the gate". Sanctuary Perspective: NeoHumans are awful, but their barter (tech, arms) is good. Spire Perspective: Useful, if annoying. CMT hates the lack of control, but a neutral hub is needed for trade and hiring deniable assets. Speculation: The only place a Longhorn manager and a Yig clan-chief might negotiate. Spires pay exorbitant fees for this neutrality and hate it. Yig vs. McGriff: Relationship: Grudging Professional Rivals. Dynamic: They are in the exact same business (underground operations). McGriff's Perspective: Yig are a nuisance ("hyper-intelligent gophers") literally eating their profit. BUT... they are uncanny prospectors. McGriff would contract Yig clans (paying in refined or non-local metals) to better locate veins or caverns. Yig's Perspective: McGriff is loud, sloppy, and wasteful (destroys the food). BUT... they crack open geodes the Yig can't, and sometimes they share. Speculation: Pure cutthroat business. Turf wars, sabotage, but also a functional trade relationship. Spires vs. Forestfolk: Spire Perspective: An obstacle. "Primitives" squatting on valuable lumber and land. To be ignored, "pacified" (bought off with cheap tech), or "reclaimed" (forcibly removed by CMT). Forestfolk Perspective: A plague. To be avoided, repelled, and sabotaged if they encroach. A danger to their lineages and forests. Spires vs. Fireborn: Spire Perspective: A high-value, high-risk industrial asset. A being that is fire? McGriff and Bröninger would kill to have a regular Fireborn workforce. Fireborn Perspective: Deeply suspicious. They were already created as a slave-labour race (by the Starborn). An "employment" offer in a Neo forge sounds eerily familiar... Spires vs. Axi & Meso Humans: Spire Perspective: "Lost cousins," failures. Axi are "deluded" (wasting tech on isolation). Meso are "backwards" (a prime market for surplus guns, source of unskilled labour). Axi & Meso Perspective: "The reason we left." Axi: Spires are "the mistake," repeating Earth's corporate ecocide. Meso: Arrogant, dangerous traders, not to be trusted for everyone's sake. Spires vs. Ar'Darun: Spire Perspective: A proprietary, peak-efficiency workforce. Seen as their creation. The most valuable manpower asset a Spire can own, count as multiple units of "manpower". Ar'Darun Perspective: "We're the ones who actually run this place." They know they were created, but they also know their skills are irreplaceable. A complex relationship of resentment and high-paid privilege. Spires vs. Houndvari: Spire Perspective: Specialized, non-human labor. A Goodlad is a born bodyguard, a Corge is a courier, a Pitmaw is expendable muscle. A resource to be "acquired". Houndvari Perspective: "A job's a job." Pragmatic. Not for everyone, that's for sure. Spires vs. Starborn: Spire Perspective: A myth. Or the ultimate prize. The researchers who know they're real are terrified at the thought. Starborn Perspective: "Unnatural." Like ants squabbling over sunlight. They do not believe Jaddivar's resources can ever be exhausted, but they distrust the methods (machinery, explosives, forest clearing) the Neo employ anyway.

item.title: AER Monster Rules
item.description: The enemies should deal enough damage to be considered threats, and take enough damage to be satisfying to dispatch. The statblocks should be lightweight, clear, and easily skimmable for info.While players get AP for their turns, it would be too troublesome to track a 1-12 value for every enemy on the battle map. As such, for the convenience of the DM, the Action Clusters were developed, monsters get limited Action Clusters. Example Action Cluster Actions would be; 1 AC cost: Move 3 Spaces and make a single weapon attack, if possible. 2 AC cost: Make a ground slam AoE attack. 4 AC cost: Open a portal to the underworld, allowing imps to flood from therein.Dominance is an original system which helps outnumbered enemies shine a bit brighter than usual. The party’s AP Regen is added together, and is divided by the sum of Enemy AC enemies gain 1 Dominance Point at the start of their turn. These allow for a couple of general Dominance Actions, as well as monster-specific ones, giving them a bit of a “last stand” once the players get the upper hand. Sum of Playerside AP Regen / Sum of Enemy Action Clusters = Dominance Points at Round Start Types: meant to give an idea to the DM skimming through the monster manual about how “important” or “influential” an enemy may be. ♕ Centrepiece. 7 AC. 5 DP. ♖ Elite. 5 AC. 3 DP. ♙ Minion. 3 AC. 1 DP.Meant to give insight into how the monster behaves in combat. Most enemies have a combination of two Roles, order does not matter, but some may have the same role twice, highlighting their focus. ♥️ - Brawler. Frontline that's tough to break through. May have area attacks. ♣️ - Commander. Buffs allies, Debuffs enemies. May summon reinforcements. ♦️ - Duellist. Single target focus, high damage, glass cannon, or all three. ♠️ - Skirmisher. Either fully ranged, with ranged capability, or simply a very mobile enemy.Hit Points, Physical and Magical Armours – the general survivability of the monster. Each of these values contributes to the overall durability.

item.title: Starborn
item.description:
The first race, made by the gods ages ago, with Aether running through their delicate frames. While humanoid from a distance, an up-close look reveals their skin to be made of carved stone, metal, or even ceramics. Their faces are smooth and featureless from the mouth up. They waged the First War and believe themselves superior to other races, especially the short-lived mortal ones. They are now mythic figures pursuing ancient agendas.... Eternal: Start with 3x the alloted starting SP.
Psychic: You perceive the world through a blindsense, being able to sense things through Cover and in all directions, but only up to 30 Hexes.
You may Concentrate (2 Action Points) to narrow Your vision into a 60 Hex line.
Divine Heritage: You are immune to Aether Sickness.

item.title: Daemons
item.description: Celestials whose halo-like head adornments have broken, now resembling tar-black horns. They have no skin, only visible muscle and bone, and can take any form as long as these two constants are maintained... Malleable: Start with ANY 2 New Magic (Flesh Shaping, Hemocrafts), General, Weapon, or Dice Manipulation Skills (1st level only, mix n' match). Silver-tongued: Gain 2x +Dice on interactions with Neutral Creatures, and -Dice on interactions with Friendly Creatures.

item.title: Psychic
item.description: Psychic: Applies -Dice to the target's next action corresponding to any damage amount greater than 1 (e.g., 2 damage becomes 1 damage and 1x -Dice). A single damage point will not apply -Dice, instead dealing damage as normal.

item.title: -Dice
item.description: Modify Resolution. Stackable. For every stack roll an extra die, then pick the lowest value rolled among the results.

item.title: +Dice
item.description: Modify Resolution. Stackable. For every stack roll an extra die, then pick the highest value rolled among the results.

item.title: Creature of the Night
item.description:
Vaguely resemblant of their old selves, these pale creatures have made the ultimate sacrifice for power and eternal life... Vampire - Bloodless: When reduced to 0 Vitals you are killed instantly (no Heroic Bleedout state).
Vampire - Unnatural Physiology: When damaged by Aether, your unnatural physiology is thrown into chaos; take the damage normally, but on the next turn, do not gain your Base Vitals Regen, gaining that value as AP and playing by the standard rules for a round instead.
Vampire - Sacrificial Power: Use Vitals in place of AP.
Any effects that interact with AP, instead interact with Vitals for you.
Eternal Thirst - Devour: Once per combat you may target an adjacent creature, if it has no Physical or Magical Armour points, deal 1 Entropy DMG to it and regain 8 Vitals. This action has no cost but instantly ends your Turn.

item.title: Yig
item.description: Furry, curled-up, hunched-over rat-like creatures with immense intelligence in their beady eyes and mineral formations on their skin. They stay underground, consuming minerals, crystals, and even rock for sustenance. They live in clan-based communities but often venture to the surface for trading or a break from their routines... Hardy: Due to mineral and/or rock consumption, start with either 4 INNATE points of Physical and 2 of Magical Armour, or 2 INNATE points of Physical and 4 of Magical Armour. When starting out, roll 1d12 to establish the amount of protrusions that result from your diet, and will be placed randomly on your inventory grid (1d12 x 1d6 for coordinates). Special Diet: Eats Ores and Minerals for sustenance. Their stomachs can handle regular food but they dislike the overall blandness of it. This includes certain items and goods, which they treat the same way as ultra-processed foods.

item.title: Neo
item.description:
Innovators and industrialists, who exploit Jaddivar and its abundance of resources paired with lack of central leadership - viewed as antagonists by the majority of other races... Human - Ambidextrous: Pick an extra Specialty when starting out. Starchart: Jaddivar-updated Northstar, but with emphasis on communication, navigation, and social status.
Certain information may be redacted, and going against the Neo ideals may even get your instance disconnected.

item.title: Meso
item.description:
Opportunists who surgically removed their implants, and inserted themselves into the existing civilisations, quickly getting familiar and accustomed with the locals and their ways of life... Human - Ambidextrous: Pick an extra Specialty when starting out
Locals: Gain +Dice on interactions with non-hostile creatures.

item.title: Axi
item.description: Part of the crash landing's population that decided not to interfere with the local order of things, they practice a Solarpunk and isolationist lifestyle, aided by the Northstar AI... Human - Ambidextrous: Pick an extra Specialty when starting out Northstar: An embedded AI-Brain chip allowing incredible information collection, recall, and thinking capabilities, as well as a user-tailored Heads-up-Display. Northstar runs on Earth-gathered data, making it inaccurate and potentially misleading when used on Jaddivar.

item.title: Ar'Darun
item.description: Shorter than humans with enlarged heads, two extra limbs, and sometimes unusual skin pigmentation, giving them an otherworldly appearance. Their origins are speculated to be the result of cross-mutation Neohuman experimental breeding programs... Extra Pair: Reduce Backpack and Equipment handling costs by 1 AP. Includes accessing items, drawing/sheathing weapons, reloading, switching ammo types.

item.title: Pitmaw
item.description:
Majestic, cow-sized canines with four paws and two arms... This one has a permanently open and panting mouth, and broad shoulders... Houndvari - Mount: You can be ridden by creatures smaller than yourself. Houndvari - Gallop: You may spend 2 AP to move 2x+1 Hexes in a straight line. Houndvari - Mule: You can Stack Backpacks of the same type.
I ain't Hear no Bell: The first time You would be reduced to or below 0 Vitals, drop down to 1 instead.

item.title: Greyhund
item.description:
Majestic, cow-sized canines with four paws and two arms... This one has an exceptionally large, and wrinkly, head, and stands tall on its paws... Houndvari - Mount: You can be ridden by creatures smaller than yourself. Houndvari - Gallop: You may spend 2 AP to move 2x+1 Hexes in a straight line. Houndvari - Mule: You can Stack Backpacks of the same type.
Old Dog, New Tricks: You may Respec Your SP during a Sanctuary Rest.

item.title: Goodlad
item.description:
Majestic, cow-sized canines with four paws and two arms... This one has very short hair and a sleek, dangerous look... Houndvari - Mount: You can be ridden by creatures smaller than Yourself. Houndvari - Gallop: You may spend 2 AP to move 2x+1 Hexes in a straight line. Houndvari - Mule: You can Stack Backpacks of the same type.
Commanding Presence: Attackers within 1 Hex of You gain -Dice on Attacks against You and Your Allies.

item.title: Dusky
item.description:
Majestic, cow-sized canines with four paws and two arms... This one has rugged and matted fur, and a long snout full of teeth... Houndvari - Mount: You can be ridden by creatures smaller than Yourself. Houndvari - Gallop: You may spend 2 AP to move 2x+1 Hexes in a straight line. Houndvari - Mule: You can Stack Backpacks of the same type.
Reckless: Your first Attack each turn costs half AP.

item.title: Corge
item.description:
Majestic, cow-sized canines with four paws and two arms... This one has short, stubby legs, and perked up triangular ears Houndvari - Mount: You can be ridden by creatures smaller than Yourself. Houndvari - Gallop: You may spend 2 AP to move 2x+1 Hexes in a straight line. Houndvari - Mule: You can Stack Backpacks of the same type.
Cavalry's Here: Allies within 1 Hex of You gain +Dice on melee Attacks.

item.title: Forestfolk
item.description: Hooved, horned, and/or clawed humanoids who emerged after wild animals consumed Aether spilled during the First War. They are adept nature dwellers and had a part in the emergence of the Houndvari, living up to their Aelf status.... Memorable Meals: You gain insight into the lives and memories of a consumed creature, clarity proportional to the body mass consumed. Quick Adaptation: The first time You take Physical or Magical DMG each combat, gain +1 Resistance to that type of DMG for the rest of that Combat.

item.title: Fireborn
item.description:
Flames bound into humanoid form, created by the Starborn for labor and metallurgy. After the First War, they revolted with the help of Forestfolk and escaped to form their own kingdoms... Light and heat source. Special Diet: You consume Fuel instead of Rations. Fire DMG restores Vitals.
Diminishing Flame: For every point of Vitals missing from Max, base Action Points Regen is reduced by 1.

item.description: Ammunition (Bullet) 1x Iron Ingot / 1x Steel Ingot / 1x Copper Ingot + 1x Iron Ingot / 1x Steel Ingot / 1x Copper Ingot => 5x Firearm Bullet Ammunition (Bolt) 1x Iron Ingot / 1x Steel Ingot + 1x Plank => 3x Crossbow Bolt Mechanical Weapon - Crossbow 2x Iron Ingot / 1x Steel Ingot + 2x Plank + 1x Fabric => Crossbow 4x Iron Ingot / 2x Steel Ingot + 3x Plank + 1x Fabric => Siege Crossbow 3x Iron Ingot / 1x Steel Ingot + 4x Plank + 4x Fabric => Repeater Crossbow Mechanical Weapon - Firearm 1x Plank + 1x Steel Ingot => Pistol 3x Plank + 2x Steel Ingot / 3x Iron Ingot => Rifle 2x Plank + 4x Steel Ingot / 6x Iron Ingot => Shotty Melee Weapon Xx Iron Ingot / X/2x Steel Ingot / Xx Gold Ingot / Xx Copper Ingot / 2Xx Scrap Metal 4Xx Wood Bundle / X Plank / X Fabric 1x Leather / 2x Bones / 2x Wood Bundle / 1x Scrap Metal / 1x Iron Ingot / 1x Steel Ingot / 1x Gold Ingot / 1x Copper Ingot 1st contribute 1:1, unlimited input. 2nd contribute 2:1, still with unlimited input. 3rd contribute 1:1, but are limited input. =<5 Spaces = Short Weapon 6-9 Spaces = Medium Weapon 10+ Spaces = Heavy WeaponEx.: 3x Iron Ingots + 12x Wood Bundles + 1x Gold Ingot = 3 + 3 (6/2) + 1 = 7 Spaces = Medium Melee Weapon. Armour (item) Size is determined by dividing the sum of its final materials (including Fabric) by 3.Ex.: 4x Iron Ingots + 12 Raw Mineral (Crystal) + 5 Fabric = 21. 21/3 = 7. The Armour has 4 Physical Pips, 12 Magical Pips, and takes up 7 inventory Spaces. OR 6x Steel Ingot + 4 Gold Ingot + 3 Fabric = 13. 13/3 = 4. The Armour has 12 Physical Pips, 8 Magical Pips, and takes up 4 inventory Spaces. Healing Item 2Xx Various Herbs / 2Xx Various Mushrooms / 2Xx Various Fruit / 4Xx Raw Meat 2Xx Various Herbs / 2Xx Various Mushrooms / 2Xx Various Fruit / 4Xx Raw Meat +2Xx Various Herbs / 2Xx Various Mushrooms / 2Xx Various Fruit / 4Xx Raw Meat Container (Empty) Various Herbs make the effect last 1 turn for every 2 Various Herbs used. Various Mushrooms make the healing effect increase by 1 every 2 Various Mushrooms used. Various Fruit increase the resulting dosage by 1 for every 2 Various Fruit used. Raw Meat can substitute any aforementioned ingredient at an increased cost. The container used when crafting will be filled with the Healing item. Multiple Containers might be necessary for large dosages as one container can only hold 5 uses.Ex.: 6x Various Herbs + 4x Various Mushrooms + 8x Raw Meat (Fruit substitute) + Empty Container = A healing effect that restores 2 HP every turn for 3 turns, and can be used 2 times. Fits in one Container. Broth Ration item. Vital Ingredient for Stew. Each line after the first is optional. 1x Water per step taken. 1x Bones / 1x Raw Meat / 1x Raw Mineral (Salt) 1x Bones / 1x Raw Meat / 1x Various Herbs 1x Bones / 1x Raw Meat / 1x Various Fruit 1x Bones / 1x Raw Meat / 1x Various Mushrooms 1x Bones / 1x Raw Meat 1x Bones / 1x Raw Meat = 1x Broth for every unique ingredient used. Jerky (1x1) Ration Item, extremely portable 3x Wood (Bundle) / 1x Raw Mineral (Coal) 1x Raw Meat / 2x Various Mushrooms / 2x Various Fruit 1x Raw Mineral (Salt) Bread (2x1) 2x Flour Bag 2x Container (Water) / 1 Container (Broth) = 2x Bread Stew Ration item. 1x Stew can count as a ration for the entire Party. 2x Broth 1x Jerky / 4x Raw Meat / 2x Raw Mineral (Salt) 2x Various Herbs / 2x Various Mushrooms / 2x Various Fruit 1x Flour Bag = 1x Stew Chunky Ore Blend Ration Item for the Yig. Converts perfectly consumable Ore into liquid form for alternative storage solutions. 1x Water 1x Raw Ore (Iron) / 1x Raw Ore (Copper) / 1x Raw Ore (Gold) 1x Raw Ore (Iron) / 1x Raw Ore (Copper) / 1x Raw Ore (Gold) 1x Raw Ore (Iron) / 1x Raw Ore (Copper) / 1x Raw Ore (Gold) = 1x Chunky Ore Blend for every unique Ore used (Requires Container). Crystal Crackers Ration item for the Yig. Sacrifices abundance of Crystal to prepare easy to stockpile Jerky alternative. (1x1) 2x Raw Mineral (Crystal) = 1x Crystal Crackers Speaking of, Crafting skill finalised. It starts with one node then splits into two, and then one of the two splits into two again.CONTAINERS ARE 1D4+1 SPACES LARGELevel 1 - Crafting. You can make use of the basic crafting Kit/Station and learn all recepies associated with it. Level 2A - Alchemy. You learn to make food items and The Healing Item. Also allows use of the Alchemy Kit/Station and recepies associated with it Level 3A - Advanced Alchemy. You learn to make advanced consumables such as specific potions (that grant resistances), and Runes (more on that another time but basically item passives limited at one per) Level 4A - SP SINK 5. Gain +1 Magical Armour Pip. Level 2B - Smelting. You learn to use the Smelting Kit/Station and make ingots from ores you find. Level 3B1 - Armoursmithing, you learn to use the Armour Smithy kit/station and the recepies associated with it Level 4B1 - Armoursmithing. You gain +1 Physical Pip. SP SINK 5. Level 3B2 - Weaponsmithing. You learn to use the anvil/weapon Smithy kit/station and make Drawn weapons (Longbow and Shortbow) as well as Arrows and Arrow Quivers, and melee weapons Level 4B2 - You learn to make mechanical weapons, their ammo and quivers/pouches to hold it I also think that attachments should occupy inventory space while unattached, AND half that amount of space when attached - but this also make the mechanical Weapon more clunky. I think it's a fair price to pay as there's otherwise no limit on attachments per weapon.Now, going a little deeper into the Runes subject. The unorganised thoughts I have in my head regarding them: - Craftable with 2 Crystal + 1 Copper Ingot / 1 Gold ingot + ANY T4 component/relic/artefact/drop (whatever they'll end up being called). Makes them relatively cheap but still scarce. Not sure whether the T4 should dictate the effects of if that should be the crafter's choice. First is more Monster Hunter-y, while second definitely can save the players some grinding - A set and specified list of 10-20 passives that can be applied to any weapon or armour. I think by default every weapon should have 1 Rune slot, BUT: 1. I don't think Mechanical weapons should get one on account of the attachments - this means putting a rune on a mechanical Weapon is significantly costlier than on any other one. 2. I think another specialised Craftable consumable that Alchemy (or maybe armoursmithing so it gets something extra to do?) could make would be a Rune Frame, which just gives +1 Rune slot. 3. To avoid 20 runes per piece of equipment, I think rune slots should have a set size/shape (like a 4x1 line, or 2x2 box), and you can only add a rune slot if it would actually fully overlap with your weapon (and not encroach on any already applied runes) +1 fire resistance / +1 Fire damage - as above with Ice, psychic, Thunder, and every other element except Aether. - +2 Blind Eyes (for the piece of equipment it's applied to, or in general?) great for You and ignoring the crystal growths - +1 AP Regen / -1 AP cost to swing/fire, maybe limited to the first attack every turn. - +1 Physical or Magical Pip / Bypass 1 Physical or Magical Pip when attacking
